mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A severe hail/wind threat continues this evening across parts of Ohio, but the need for a downstream watch remains uncertain

details.label: Summary
details.text: A severe hail/wind threat continues this evening across parts of Ohio, but the need for a downstream watch remains uncertain

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Two slow-moving clusters have become the primary severe risk this evening across western OH. While a very unstable airmass remains in place ahead of this activity (MLCAPE up to 3000-3500+ J/kg per recent mesoanalysis), a lack of recent wind reports suggests that these thunderstorms may be slightly elevated. Even so, modest low-level southwesterlies veering to west-northwesterly and gradually strengthening with height through mid levels will continue to foster around 30-35 kt of deep-layer shear (reference the 00Z ILN observed sounding). This should be sufficient for continued updraft organization, with occasional severe/damaging winds the primary threat given the ongoing cluster mode. Isolated hail also appears possible with embedded stronger cores. These clusters will spread east-southeastward this evening across central OH, and will eventually encounter a less unstable airmass into far eastern OH and WV, where prior convective overturning occurred earlier today. Therefore, the potential for organized severe convection persisting east of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 560 remains uncertain, as does the need for a downstream watch

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for very large hail and severe winds will continue as a robust supercell migrates southeast across western South Dakota

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Over the past hour, a lone, but intense, supercell has exhibited persistent three-body scatter spikes consistent with very large hail, and has also produced wind gusts of at least 61 mph per recent reports. More recently, the reflectivity core has diminished slightly, and the storm motion has shifted from due south to southeasterly, suggesting a slight weakening of the storm's internal pressure perturbations and overall intensity. However, this cell will continue to reside within an environment very favorable for intense convection (MLCAPE near 4000 J/kg and nearly 50 knots of effective bulk shear as sampled by the 00 UTC UNR and ABR soundings), so some degree of re-intensification appears possible. Additionally, new updraft development is noted on the western flank of the cell, which may also intensify and pose a threat for very large (2 inch) hail and severe gusts. Given the elongated/straight nature of regional wind profiles, the emergence of this new cell hints that cell interactions and cold pool amalgamation may increase over the next couple of hours as the new cell begins to split. This may result in a very gradual transition from a supercellular to a clustered/linear storm mode with an attendant increase in severe wind potential as storms move further south/southeast. A few recent high-res solutions hint at this transition, but confidence in this scenario is somewhat limited at this point due to the isolated nature of the convection

statements.headline: Severe Weather Statement
statements.summary: Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees. Locations impacted include... Wheeling, Martins Ferry, St. Clairsville, Warwood, Bethlehem, West Liberty, Triadelphia, Clearview, Valley Grove, Tiltonsville, Bridgeport, Yorkville, Bethany, Smithfield, Adena, Dillonvale, Brookside and Beech Bottom.
